Identify the Minimum Sample Size Meeting Specified Criteria

Source: R/pmgen_summarise.R
pmgen_min_n.Rd

Scans the posterior summaries and raw draws in a pmgen_result object and returns the smallest N at which all user-specified criteria are simultaneously met.

Usage

pmgen_min_n(result, criteria = list(), ...)

Arguments

result

A pmgen_result object from pmgen_simulate().

criteria

Named list of criterion specifications. The name must match a metric computed in result (e.g. "cstat", "cal_slope", "mape", "net_benefit", "ervsi"). Each element is itself a named list choosing one criterion type:

range + min_prob

P(metric in range) >= min_prob. Use for calibration slope: list(range = c(0.9, 1.1), min_prob = 0.90).

max_mean

mean(metric) <= max_mean (for lower-is-better metrics like MAPE, or absolute degradation). E.g. list(max_mean = 0.05).

min_mean

mean(metric) >= min_mean. E.g. list(min_mean = 0.70) for c-statistic floor.

max_abs_deg_mean

|mean degradation| <= threshold. Uses degradation_mean from summaries. E.g. list(max_abs_deg_mean = 0.025).

min_prob_above

P(metric >= threshold) >= min_prob. E.g. for ERVSI: list(min_prob_above = 0.90, min_prob = 0.90).

min_prob_below

P(metric <= threshold) >= min_prob. E.g. list(min_prob_below = 0.05, min_prob = 0.90) for MAPE.

...

Reserved for future arguments.

Value

An object of class pmgen_min_n, a list with:

min_n

The smallest N meeting all criteria, or NA if none do.

table

Data frame: one row per N, one column per criterion, plus all_met (logical) and N.

criteria

The criteria list as supplied.

References

Riley RD, Whittle R, Sadatsafavi M, Martin GP, Pate A, Collins GS, Ensor J. A general sample size framework for developing or updating a predictive algorithm: with application to clinical prediction models. BMC Medical Research Methodology. 2026;26:121. doi:10.1186/s12874-026-02856-7

Examples

# Small settings so the example runs quickly; see pmgen_simulate()
ref <- pmgen_reference(
  joint_data = dvt_data, predictors = setdiff(names(dvt_data), "dvt"),
  prevalence = 0.21, cstatistic = 0.78,
  n_bisect_pop = 1e5, n_synth = 1e5, seed = 42
)
#> Running bisection to calibrate reference model...
#> Bisection converged: prevalence=0.2100 (target=0.2100), c-stat=0.7791 (target=0.7800)
#> Unit information matrix computed and cached.
tp <- pmgen_target_population(ref, n = 5000, seed = 42)
result <- pmgen_simulate(ref, tp, N = c(250, 1000), n_sims = 20,
                         metrics = c("cstat", "cal_slope", "mape"),
                         seed = 1, verbose = FALSE)

pmgen_min_n(result, criteria = list(
  cal_slope = list(range = c(0.8, 1.2), min_prob = 0.80),
  mape      = list(max_mean = 0.05)
))
#> pmgen minimum sample size
#> -------------------------
#>   Minimum N : 1000
#> 
#> Criterion compliance by N:
#>     N cal_slope mape all_met
#>   250       no   no      no 
#>  1000       YES  YES     YES
